CLOUD realm: walked all 25 real dirs against the 25 taxonomy substrate groups. Set diff is empty in BOTH directions: zero cloud/ dirs missing from the taxonomy, and zero taxonomy substrate groups without a backing real dir. Perfect 1:1 mapping.

NO MISSING DIRECTORIES in either realm. The taxonomy's products (87) and substrates (25) groups fully and exactly cover the real /Users/jasonlee/Developer/source/oya/ and /Users/jasonlee/Developer/source/cloud/ directory trees.

verification.check: Taxonomy CONSISTENCY: (1) every product/substrate in exactly one category; (2) every microservice has >=1 layer; (3) adapters have port+tech; (4) no duplicate microservice slugs across groups; (5) status values valid. Note: the input JSON was truncated after the realms array (dogfood_edges cut off), but the entire realms structure that these checks operate on is complete, so all five checks were evaluated in full.

None are status=built (all stub or spec-only), so the violation is confined to catalog-scaffold/spec-only entries — but the check as stated has no status carve-out.

CHECK 1 (every product/substrate in exactly one category) — PASS. No group slug appears under more than one (realm,category); no group mixes product/substrate kind. 110 distinct groups carry microservices; the 2 zero-microservice products (app-shell-frontend, social) each sit in exactly one category (Workspace & Collaboration).

CHECK 3 (adapters have port+tech) — PASS by literal reading. All 146 adapters in the body have non-empty port and tech. Caveat: several use placeholder values that are non-empty but non-descriptive — port/tech '(generic)' (ops-docs-portal, ops-workspace-shell, observability-tracing, plugin-app-store audit-stream) and 'unspecified' (api-gateway-routing, consent-graph-agreement, and the 4 governance-* adapters). These pass 'has port+tech' but are semantically empty placeholders; flag if the intent is that port/tech be concrete.
CHECK 4 (no duplicate microservice slugs across groups) — PASS. 208 microservices parsed, 208 unique slugs, zero collisions across groups or realms.
CHECK 5 (status values valid: built | stub | spec-only) — PASS. Every microservice carries one of the three valid status values; no invalid/unknown status found.

EXTRA INTEGRITY ISSUE — header counts do not match the body. Declared counts say microservices=210 and adapters=148, but the realms body enumerates 208 microservices and 146 adapters (a shortfall of 2 each). Declared products=87 and substrates=25 should also be reconciled against the body. The two zero-microservice products (app-shell-frontend, social) do not close the microservice gap since they contribute no microservices. This is a counts-vs-body inconsistency separate from the five requested checks.
